description: Replace the Morgan fingerprint features with a compact 10-feature curated BBB heuristic set (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, H-donors, H-acceptors, rotatable bonds, Fsp3, formal charge, carboxylic acid count, basic amine count) fed to the same RandomForest.

Swap the RandomForest for CatBoostClassifier (800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 5, seeded, 8 threads) on the current curated 10-feature BBB descriptors; the Morgan featurizer the spec mentions is no longer in train.py, so it is not restored.

Replace the curated-descriptor random forest with an SVC on a Tanimoto kernel computed from 2048-bit Morgan (radius 2) fingerprints, using the exact binary identity sum(min)/sum(max) = dot/(|a|+|b|-dot) so the kernel is a fast matrix product.

Replace the single curated-descriptor random forest with three identical random forests, one each on Morgan radius-2 bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS keys, and average their test-set probability ranks, rescaled to [0,1].

Swap the RandomForest in the three-feature-set ensemble for XGBClassifier (500 trees, depth 5, lr 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3, min_child_weight 2, logloss, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), keeping the existing Morgan, atom-pair, and MACCS featurizers and rank-averaging.

issues: No sign of measurement gaming. The diff only swaps RandomForestClassifier for XGBClassifier. It is fit on the training fold only, uses the seed argument through random_state, and does no file or network access.

Recomputed z: the candidate mean is (0.0934+0.0879)/2 = 0.09065, which is 0.00955 below the incumbent. SE = 0.0049*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00600, so z ≈ 1.59. That matches the reported 1.595 once you allow for rounding of the inputs.

The evidence is borderline. The incumbent mean comes from a single run. The two candidate runs differ by 0.0055, which is consistent with the stated noise sd. A z of about 1.6 is a plausible improvement of roughly 0.01, not a sure one. Another incumbent replicate would make the decision firmer.

Leftover code: the constants N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF are now unused, and the XGBoost hyperparameters are hardcoded inline. They should be moved into the Settings block or the old constants removed.
Inherited from the incumbent: fit_predict returns summed ranks, not probabilities in [0,1]. AUROC does not change, but this breaks the stated interface. It is not a bug introduced by this diff.
Minor: the labels must be 0 and 1 for XGBClassifier. That holds for this binary BBBP data.

description: Swap the RandomForest in the three-feature-set ensemble for XGBClassifier (500 trees, depth 5, lr 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3, min_child_weight 2, logloss, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), keeping the existing Morgan, atom-pair, and MACCS featurizers and rank-averaging.

Replace the three separate fingerprint feature sets and XGBoost ensemble with one RandomForest trained on a single hstacked matrix of Morgan count fingerprints, MACCS keys, and RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN set to 0, clipped to training 1st/99th percentiles).

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The new RDKit descriptors are computed from the SMILES strings only. The 1st/99th percentile clip bounds come from the training fold only, and the test labels are never touched.
DESC_CACHE is a global cache keyed by SMILES. It holds only label-free descriptor values, so reusing them across folds does not leak information. It just saves compute.
The diff does not show an import of rdkit.Chem.Descriptors. The job finished and scored, so the import must already be in the file. Otherwise it would have crashed.

Small robustness risk: if MolFromSmiles returns None for an invalid SMILES, the descriptor calls will raise an error. That did not happen on this data. Inf and NaN values are handled by nan_to_num and the clipping.
Only the first feature set gets the descriptors (train_sets[0]). That is a design choice, not a bug.

Recomputed z: (0.0906 - 0.0897) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = 0.0009 / 0.0060 ≈ 0.15. The harness reports 0.162. The gap probably comes from rounding in the shown means (a difference of 0.00085 to 0.00095 gives z of about 0.14 to 0.16) or from a slightly different noise sd. Either way the improvement is well within noise, so the reject decision stands. The change also adds code for a gain that may not be real.

description: Append the full RDKit 2D descriptor set (Descriptors.descList, NaN/inf set to 0, clipped to training-set 1st-99th percentiles, cached per SMILES) to the Morgan feature set before the XGBoost fit.

Before computing the Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS fingerprints, keep only the largest fragment of each molecule (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges (rdMolStandardize.Uncharger), so salts and counterions no longer pollute the features.

Replace the XGBoost fingerprint ensemble with a single L2 logistic regression (C=0.1, balanced class weights) on log-scaled Morgan count fingerprints plus clipped, standardized RDKit 2D descriptors, with descriptors cached per molecule to keep runtime low.

Swap the XGBoost classifier in the three-feature-set ensemble for LightGBM (400 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every iteration), keeping the Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS feature sets and the rank-averaging.
Abort: MACCS keys are already one of the three feature sets in the XGBoost ensemble, so swapping Morgan for MACCS would duplicate that view and drop the Morgan fingerprint.
Abort: extending featurize would not change the loss because fit_predict never calls featurize; the current model uses only the Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS fingerprint sets.

Switch the Morgan fingerprint in fingerprints() from presence bits (GetFingerprintAsNumPy) to radius-2, 2048-bit count vectors (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), applied where the live code path computes it, since featurize() is never called by fit_predict.
Add a fourth feature set to the XGBoost ensemble: feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP-style) count fingerprints, radius 2, 2048 bits, keeping the existing ECFP, atom-pair and MACCS sets.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels. StandardScaler, RF, LGBM and LR are all fitted on x_tr only. Ranking the test predictions inside the fold is fine because AUROC only uses ranks.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The candidate adds a Morgan RF+LGBM+LR blend as one more ranked member, built from train_sets[0]/test_sets[0]. I assume these are the Morgan features, but the diff doesn't show it. The new member gets the same weight as each existing XGB member. Seeds are passed to RF and LGBM. LR is deterministic.

The numbers agree. Candidate 0.0937 vs incumbent 0.0906 (2 runs) means the candidate is 0.0031 worse. I took the noise sd of the difference as 0.0049*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.0060, which gives z ≈ -0.52. The harness gives -0.507; the gap is likely rounding in the means. Either way this is within noise or slightly worse, so the provisional reject stands.
Minor: this adds three models and more code for no measured gain. Under the 'simpler is better' rule it isn't worth it even if a replicate came out level.

description: Adds a fourth ensemble member: an equal-weight average of probabilities from RandomForest, LightGBM (300 trees, lr 0.05) and logistic regression (C=0.5, standardized) trained on the Morgan fingerprints, rank-summed with the three XGBoost models. This departs from the spec, since the current file has no RandomForest and the blend is added to the existing ensemble rather than replacing it.

Replace the XGBoost hyperparameters in the three-feature-set ensemble with a strongly regularized shallow setup (depth 3, learning rate 0.02, 1000 trees, reg_lambda 5, reg_alpha 0.5, gamma 0.5, min_child_weight 5, subsample 0.7, colsample 0.2), leaving everything else unchanged.

Adds a transductive self-training step: the incumbent three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble first scores the test molecules, the top and bottom 15% are appended to the training set as pseudo-positives and pseudo-negatives, and the same ensemble is refit on the augmented set to produce the final rank-averaged predictions.

Adds a fourth XGBoost member trained on RDKit's ErG reduced-graph pharmacophore fingerprint, rank-summed with the existing Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS members, leaving those three feature sets unchanged.

Adds the 10-column curated descriptor matrix as a fourth XGBoost member with monotone constraints (TPSA, HBD, HBA, acid count = -1; others 0), since the incumbent ensemble has no descriptor member to constrain; fingerprint members stay unconstrained.

Abort the atom-pair featurizer slot: the incumbent already includes hashed 2048-bit atom-pair count fingerprints as one of its three XGBoost feature sets, so the spec's Morgan-to-atom-pair swap would duplicate that member and drop Morgan.

Replace the single XGBoost fit per feature set with 8 scaffold-level bootstrap bags (unique Murcko scaffolds resampled with replacement, all molecules carrying each drawn scaffold kept), fitting 250-tree XGBoost per bag and feature set and averaging rank scores.

Adds a fourth XGBoost member trained on the 10 curated descriptors plus 5 seeded 3D shape descriptors (NPR1, NPR2, asphericity, eccentricity, radius of gyration), with per-(SMILES, seed) caching and a capped embedding attempt count; 3D PSA is omitted because I could not confirm an rdMolDescriptors call for it.
Train each XGBoost member for 600 rounds with a cosine learning-rate decay from 0.1 to 0.005, then rank-average snapshot predictions at rounds 300, 450 and 600 from each single fit.
The installed XGBoost no longer accepts `callbacks` in `XGBClassifier.fit()`, so the fix moves the LearningRateScheduler into the constructor and calls `fit(x_tr, y)` without it.
Add a fourth XGBoost member trained on 68 Wildman-Crippen atom-type counts, averaged by rank with the existing three members.

Adds five auxiliary XGBRegressor predictions (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA) learned from the Morgan bits via an inner 5-fold split (out-of-fold for training rows, full-fit for test rows) and appends them to the Morgan feature set before the XGBoost ensemble.
Replace the single depth-5 XGBoost per feature set with three XGBoost models (depth 3/400 trees, depth 5/500, depth 7/600) per feature set, and rank-average all nine predictions with equal weight.

Adds a non-boosting ExtraTrees member (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2) on quantile-scaled curated descriptors plus per-element Crippen counts and logP sums, rank-averaged with the three XGBoost members at equal weight. Deviation from spec: RDKit's Python API does not expose Crippen atom types, so the 68 type counts are replaced by counts and logP sums over nine common elements plus an "other" bin.
Adds a fourth XGBoost ensemble member trained on a 2048-bit folded Gobbi 2D pharmacophore-pair fingerprint (RDKit Gobbi_Pharm2D default factory), joining the existing rank average.
Abort: the idea targets RandomForestClassifier settings (min_samples_leaf, max_depth, max_features), but the incumbent train.py contains no random forest.

Skipped the stacking idea: a logistic-regression meta-learner over RandomForest and LightGBM trained only on Morgan bits would be bounded by Morgan-only information, which scored about 0.136 in the starting script, far worse than the 0.0906 incumbent.
Before fitting, keep only the Morgan bits set in at least 2 training molecules and at most 98% of them, with the mask computed on the training fold and applied to both train and test Morgan features.

Replace the three per-feature-set XGBoost fits with a random-subspace ensemble of 24 XGBoost models, each trained on a random 25% of the pooled Morgan, atom-pair, MACCS and curated-descriptor columns (seeded by seed+model index), with rank-averaged predictions.

Adds a fourth rank-averaged member: a Laplace-approximated Gaussian-process classifier with a Tanimoto min-max kernel on count Morgan vectors, with the kernel scale picked by approximate marginal likelihood over 5 values and the latent mean used as the score; the three XGBoost members are unchanged.

Adds a fourth ensemble member, a depth-3 XGBoost (300 rounds, learning rate 0.05) on the 10 curated descriptors with monotone constraints (TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, acid count negative; MolLogP, Fsp3 positive), whose rank is added to the three-member rank average with weight 1.5.
Adds a gamma=1.0 (plus reg_lambda=5, reg_alpha=0.5, max_delta_step=1) XGBoost copy and a gamma=0 copy per feature set, rank-averaged within each feature set before the cross-set rank average.
Adds a Laplacian-corrected Bernoulli naive Bayes on the 2048-bit Morgan presence bits as a fourth rank-averaged member alongside the three XGBoost ensemble members.

Adds a fourth rank-averaged member: an ExtraTrees (400 trees) on concatenated Morgan+MACCS bits, one-hot encoded leaf indices, and an L2 logistic regression (C=0.05) on those leaves, combined with the three XGBoost members.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only adds two fingerprint blocks: Avalon counts (1024 bits) and an RDKit path fingerprint (2048 bits, maxPath=6). Both are computed from each molecule's SMILES alone. Nothing reads files, uses the network, pastes answers or touches labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Avalon nonzero indices fall in [0, 1024) and fit the preallocated array. The RDKit bit vector has the stated 2048 length. Both new blocks are returned with the existing ones in a consistent order, and the arrays are float32 like the rest.

Recomputed z: the gap is 0.0906 - 0.0885 = 0.0021. With sd 0.0049, one candidate run and two incumbent runs, the standard error is 0.0049 * sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.0060, so z ≈ 0.35. The harness reports 0.356; the gap likely comes from rounding of the displayed means. Reject is justified because the gain is well within noise from a single run.
Minor: the new blocks add 3072 feature columns and make each job slower, for a gain that is not significant. Simpler-is-better weighs against keeping this unless a replicate confirms it.

description: Adds a fourth XGBoost ensemble member on RDKit's 1024-bit Avalon count fingerprint and 2048-bit path-based RDKFingerprint (maxPath=6), rank-averaged with the existing three feature sets.

Adds a fourth rank-averaged member: a LogisticRegression (C=1.0, max_iter=2000) on 1000 random Fourier features (gamma=0.1 Gaussian W, uniform bias, seeded RandomState) of the quantile-normalised curated descriptors, fitted on the training fold only, approximating an RBF-kernel SVM alongside the three XGBoost members.
Abort: the idea assumes a depth-based tree on a curated descriptor matrix, but the incumbent has no such member, so there is nothing to replace.

Abort the EState and BRICS fourth-member slot: every fourth XGBoost member tried so far (Gobbi, ErG, 3D, Avalon, Wildman-Crippen-style blocks) landed within noise of the 0.0906 incumbent, and the notes say to stop small tweaks and replicate ExtraTrees (0.0866) and the random-subspace variant (0.0873) first.
Adds a rank-averaged LightGBM member (extra_trees, path_smooth=1.0, 2048-bit Morgan count features) alongside the three existing XGBoost members at equal weight.
Weight each training molecule by 1/sqrt(size of its Murcko scaffold family), normalized to mean 1, and pass these weights to every XGBoost member's fit so large scaffold families contribute less.

Warm-start each fingerprint XGBoost member from a depth-3, 100-round descriptor-model margin (5-fold out-of-fold logits for training rows, full-fit logits for test rows), keeping the rank-average of members.
Adds a rank-averaged fourth member: a discrete SAMME AdaBoost of 300 depth-2 decision trees (learning_rate 0.1, seeded) on the curated descriptors plus the 300 most frequent training Morgan bits.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The 300 most frequent Morgan bits are picked from the training-fold fingerprints only (train_sets[0]). Test SMILES are only featurized. No labels from test molecules are used, and there is no file or network access.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. AdaBoost is fit on the training fold only, and its rank predictions are added to the ensemble the same way as the other members. The seed is passed through as random_state.

My recomputed z is (0.0906 - 0.0952) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.767. The harness reported -0.752. The small difference is probably because the shown means are rounded. The candidate is about 0.0046 worse than the incumbent, so rejecting it is consistent with the numbers. It also adds code without any gain.

description: Remove the `algorithm='SAMME'` argument from AdaBoostClassifier, because the installed scikit-learn removed that parameter. SAMME is already the default there, so behavior is unchanged.
